nodes.title: Mark Axelus
nodes.summary: 4th-year Computer Science at UVic, Victoria BC. Junior software engineer at OceanAID. Working toward a startup and Next 36.
nodes.body:
- he/him. GitHub markaxelus. markaxelus.com.
- Full-stack and AI/ML. Best at making things actually work, end to end.
- Building things since 2019.
- Hackathons for the fun and the adrenaline: nwHacks every January since 2024, Hack the North 2026.

nodes.title: Startup path
nodes.summary: The plan: get something real going, apply to Next 36 next rotation, do the 8-month cohort in Toronto, then decide. Under all of it: be in a room of truly ambitious people.
nodes.body:
1. Something going. A startup with compounding impact, built at my own pace.
2. Next 36, next rotation. Proof of being qualified and the door into the right environment.
3. Toronto, 8 months.
4. After that: open.

Leaning toward Base 36 as the immediate step. Unconfirmed.

nodes.title: Be in a room of truly ambitious people
nodes.summary: The want under everything else. Rooms like Hack the North, where people build things that should exist. Even if an idea fails there, the environment is right.
nodes.body:
- HTN 2026: energized on almost no sleep, wanted to keep building.
- UVic does not give this. Known for a long time, undeniable after HTN.
- Routes: a startup that is actually going, Next 36 in Toronto, Waterloo-level people.

nodes.title: How to get ahead into those environments?
nodes.summary: Asked right after HTN. Hackathons are not it. Open.

nodes.title: Start a startup with compounding impact
nodes.summary: AI-related, hard, unsolved. A small app with a thousand users is not enough. A great product speaks for itself.
nodes.body:
- It should be obvious why it exists.
- Live in a problem nobody else tackles because it is too hard.
- Reference point: Arga Labs raised a $10M pre-seed.

nodes.title: What is the startup idea?
nodes.summary: Still missing as of Sept 2026. Wants AI, hard, unsolved, compounding. Ideas so far felt superficial.
nodes.body: Explored: Reclaim and Telco (legal-complaint tooling; someone else's acquisition play, doubts about retention). The compliance idea in Startup Studio, skeptical.

nodes.title: The next startup is not marine tech
nodes.summary: Do not want to deal with marine tech or copy what OceanAID does.

nodes.title: Build at my own pace, not the class's
nodes.summary: Not waiting for the Startup Studio team. Ship on my own timeline.

nodes.title: Find co-founders
nodes.summary: The biggest thing. Ambitious people who want to go far and keep building past the weekend.
nodes.body:
- HTN 2026 was a co-founder search first: 'even if we don't win I'd be walking out with 3 co-founders.'
- Team shape wanted: 3 (one woman, one man) or 4 (two and two).
- Looking for people who get excited by ambitious ideas, are easy to be around, open, take ownership, communicate.

nodes.title: Co-founders over demos
nodes.summary: Staying power past the weekend beats weekend execution speed. Ambition is the filter.

nodes.title: OceanAID
nodes.summary: Marine-tech startup in Victoria. Junior Software Engineer, there by May 2026 (start date not recorded). Built and run the production system end to end.

nodes.body:

nodes.title: Dockside
nodes.summary: A miniature Marlin Box: edge computer vision for marine debris with cloud training and offline-first telemetry. Built to learn Ultralytics, CUDA, Jetson and AWS by rebuilding OceanAID's architecture on a laptop.
nodes.body: Roboflow dataset, YOLOv8 training on EC2, TensorRT edge inference, SQLite offline buffer, Lambda and DynamoDB, dashboard. Five checkpoints.

nodes.title: Self-knowledge
nodes.summary: What I know about how I work.
nodes.body:
- Perseverance over raw technical ability.
- Energized by ambitious rooms.
- I do the work without being told.
- Hard to frame what I have done.

nodes.title: Perseverance is the edge
nodes.summary: 'I'll work harder than anyone because I don't have anything.' Technical ability is not the differentiator yet. Wanting things to work, and doing whatever it takes, is.

nodes.title: I do the work without being told
nodes.summary: Rely on me to do the things no one else wants to do, or figure out what no one knows how to do. On shared projects I end up doing all the work.

nodes.title: How to frame what I have done?
nodes.summary: Hard to collect the work and present it convincingly. The resume does not look like the Waterloo people's. What I have to offer, and what I look for in others, is not yet clear to me.
